latestChangelog:
This alpha introduces HiGHS optimization in both the browser and Windows app,
with live results and more control over practical pile-plan coherence. It also
makes the inspection panels and pile-option tables easier to customize.

### Added

- Minimize pile-plan costs within configurable tip-level, size and configuration
  limits, or minimize differences between neighboring units within a cost budget.
  The default additional-cost budget is 5%; configuration limits default to unlimited.
- Use Quick improve for a local improvement without waiting for a full spatial
  solve. Feasible current plans and improved starting solutions help warm-start
  the solver.
- Follow the best validated solution live, with its score, lower bound and gap.
  View another pile plan while optimization continues, stop and use the best
  result, or cancel and discard the preview. Completed results belong to the plan.
- Choose specific candidate configurations using a matrix with row and column
  selection, and optionally skip locations that have no valid configuration.
- Inspect load points and CPTs together using the optional split view, with
  compact CPT details and a resizable divider whose position is remembered.
- Show, hide and drag-reorder pile-option columns. Preferences are remembered
  separately for single-location and multiple-location selections.
- Return from input sources to the active pile plan with a close button, keeping
  the current selection and viewport.

### Improved and fixed

- Replace the former greedy optimizer with one optimization panel. Use collapsible
  settings, clearer result quality, named output plans and preserved selections.
- Reject non-positive net design resistance as an unavailable pile option rather
  than accepting negative utilization.
- Improve warning text and link contrast, themed controls, numeric field stepping,
  validation styling and compact panel spacing.
- Refresh application dependencies.

### Compatibility and limitations

- Supported older IFCPP projects continue to open; legacy optimizer settings are
  normalized. New projects and saved optimizer outcomes use the current project format.
- Browser and desktop use the same Rust optimization model, solved by HiGHS.
  Search progress and run time can differ between platforms.
- Quick improvement does not prove global optimality. A solver stopped early or
  at its time limit returns the best validated result available, with its quality
  reported separately from the cost reference.
- This remains an alpha release; engineering results require professional review.

releases.name: Pile Plan Studio v0.3.0-alpha
changes: Visualize connected pile-tip-level regions in the plan viewer.
Treat nearby load points as assignment groups. Manual pile changes, default selection, locking, and greedy optimization apply one common configuration to the complete group.
Compare aggregated pile options for multiple selected load points, including maximum utilization and the governing load point.
Inspect and navigate to CPTs whose bearing-capacity data is missing for a configuration.
Clearly distinguish missing bearing-capacity data, insufficient capacity, permanent group conflicts, and configurations excluded by optimizer settings.
Report unresolved optimization results by both load point and group, while keeping permanent technical conflicts separate from optimizer failures.
Make Undo and Redo predictable for symbol-size and preferred-utilization slider changes.
The optimizer remains a deterministic greedy heuristic and does not guarantee a global optimum. A future optimization method is tracked separately.

releases.name: Pile Plan Studio 0.1.8-alpha
changes: Undo and redo persisted project changes, with concise feedback in the viewer.
Recover the latest browser project from IndexedDB after an accidental refresh or interrupted session.
Resize the project explorer horizontally using the same lightweight behavior as the properties panel.
Excel and CSV export the active pile plan and use its name as the suggested file name.
Importing a standard or Legacy pile-plan table creates and activates a new named pile plan while preserving existing plans.
Pile-cost defaults come from the bundled sample project and no longer change silently across projects.
Permanent inspection tabs close open settings panels, while viewer selection keeps them available.
Browser recovery is a convenience safeguard, not a replacement for saving an IFCPP project.
Excel and CSV contain one active pile plan; IFCPP preserves the complete project with all pile plans.
No Windows installer is included in this release while signing setup remains unavailable.

releases.name: Pile Plan Studio 0.1.7-alpha
changes: Lock and unlock load points per pile plan. Locked locations remain visible but dimmed, cannot be selected during ordinary plan editing, and are ignored by greedy optimization.
Edit locked locations directly in the viewer using click and lasso interactions, with Apply, Cancel, and Unlock all controls.
Show grid lines aligned to actual project coordinates, with adaptive spacing and a View-ribbon toggle.
Consolidated project, plan, inspection, settings, locking, and optimization actions into a clearer ribbon layout.
CPT, cost, and optimization settings now open as dedicated task panels.
Optimization, pile head level, and CPT number fields now allow temporary empty editing before validation on Enter or blur.
The feedback dialog accepts every non-empty message and opens issues in the Pile Plan Studio repository.
This prerelease does not include a Windows installer. The browser build and source code contain the 0.1.7-alpha changes.
